SELECTED_INDEX: 1  
CONFIDENCE: 0.38  
EXPLANATION: The spectrum shows (a) a very strong C=O stretch at 1817 cm⁻¹ – characteristic of acyl fluorides, whose ν(C=O) appears near 1810-1820 cm⁻¹, far higher than the 1700-1760 cm⁻¹ region of ordinary ketones and lactones; (b) intense aliphatic C–H stretches at 2880-2970 cm⁻¹ and CH₃ deformations at 1458/1418 cm⁻¹, consistent with a small aliphatic acyl fragment (CH₃CH₂–); (c) strong bands at 1108 and 1065 cm⁻¹ assignable to C–O and O–F/C–F stretches typical for acyl fluorides; (d) a prominent band at 713 cm⁻¹ that matches reported O–F stretching frequencies (~700-750 cm⁻¹). Among the candidates only molecule 1 (CCC(=O)OF, propionyl hypofluorite / propanoyl fluoride) contains the acyl-fluoride functional group and an aliphatic chain, fully accounting for all key Raman features, whereas the other candidates either lack fluorine or possess carbonyl groups that would give the C=O stretch far below 1817 cm⁻¹.
